event.centerRule: The four Gospel witnesses remain distinct Scripture evidence. The Event is not reconstructed by silently filling one account from another. Earlier Passover and covenant sources, immediate departure scenes, and later remembrance are connected only through explicit quotation, vocabulary, narrative setting, or analytical comparison.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus Christ
characterAnchors.note: Hosts and interprets the meal, serves the disciples, exposes betrayal, teaches, prays, and goes toward arrest.

characterAnchors.label: Peter
characterAnchors.note: Prepares the room in Luke, resists washing, claims loyalty, receives warning and prayer, sleeps, and uses the sword.

characterAnchors.label: Judas Iscariot
characterAnchors.note: Agrees to betray Jesus, remains within the table sayings, receives the morsel in John, and leaves into night.

characterAnchors.label: The beloved disciple
characterAnchors.note: Receives Peter’s signal and asks Jesus whom he means in John’s betrayer scene.

characterAnchors.label: The Twelve / apostles / disciples
characterAnchors.note: Prepare, recline, question, eat, drink, dispute, receive commands and promises, and move toward scattering.

characterAnchors.label: The Father
characterAnchors.note: Is named throughout the farewell teaching and prayer as sender, giver, lover, glorifier, and the one whose will Jesus accepts.

characterAnchors.label: The Corinthian assembly
characterAnchors.note: Receives Paul’s tradition and correction about participation, division, discernment, and waiting.

event.throughline: Passover approaches; Jesus prepares and reclines with his disciples; betrayal is disclosed; bread, cup, service, love, departure, and denial are interpreted; extended farewell teaching and prayer lead toward arrest; Pauline communities receive and practice the meal under communal scrutiny.

topic.orientation: Enter the final meal through four distinct witnesses. Passover and covenant sources prepare the language; Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John preserve their own sequences; John’s farewell teaching and prayer deepen the night; Paul and later sources show how the meal is remembered, practiced, and compared.
